# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

Now I have exact rules:

**CRAP = CC² × (1 − coverage)³ + CC**

- At 0% coverage: CC² + CC ✓ (matches ticket).
- At 100% coverage: CRAP = CC. So a fully-covered function has CRAP = its CC!
- Threshold 8: new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8.
  - CC 3 fully covered → CRAP 3 ✓. CC 9 fully covered → 9 ✗.
  - CC 2 untested → 4+2 = 6 ✓. CC 3 untested → 9+3=12 ✗.

So new helpers with CC up to ~8-9 are fine IF fully covered; untested helpers need CC ≤ 2.

**Cyclomatic CC counts (base 1, +1 each):** If, For, ForIn, ForOf, While, DoWhile, **CatchClause**, SwitchCase, ConditionalExpression, **LogicalExpression (&& and ||)**. Named nested FunctionDeclarations are skipped (counted as their own entries).

Now verify baseline TA: CRAP 1177.1. Coverage x: CC 33: 1089u³+33 = 1177.1 → u³ = 1.0497 → u > 1 impossible. CC 34: 1156u³ + 34 = 1177.1 → u³ = 0.9888 → u = 0.99626 → cov = 0.37%. Hmm, that means TA action had ~0.4% coverage in the baseline?? Ticket says 54% covered. Hmm — coverage here is STATEMENT coverage per function from Istanbul... The wave2d1 test exercises action via jira path... maybe that test was added after the baseline was released. The baseline is rolling (min(old, now)) — released at some past commit. Ticket numbers CC 105/CRAP 1177.1 might come from a different measurement (ticket.json says CC 105, 54%). Baseline says the action CC is likely ~34? Hmm wait — maybe coverage in the baseline run was 0 (function only covered by tests added later?). The current tree HAS the wave2d1/wave2d4 tests covering action paths. If the current measurement shows action CRAP << baseline, then the ratchet sees improvement already. 

Whatever — the gate: vs released baseline: `js/triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action` baseline 1177.1 must go DOWN; no function may go UP; new functions CRAP ≤ 8.

CRAP 303.5 iOS: CC 17: 289u³+17 = 303.5 → u³ = 0.9914 → u=0.99713 → cov 0.29%. So in the baseline both actions were essentially uncovered (the wave2d* tests must postdate the baseline, or the baseline run's instrumented harness failed to cover them). CC values: TA CC ≈ 34, iOS CC ≈ 17. (Ticket's "CC 105" doesn't match this tool's counting — ticket numbers were approximate from another tool. Fine.)

Target: both actions below CRAP 50:
- Fully covered CC 7 → CRAP 7 ✓. CC 10 → 10 ✓. CC 49 → 49 ✓ (if fully covered!). Interesting — with 100% coverage CRAP = CC, so "under 50" means CC < 50 when fully covered! That's much easier than I feared.

But careful: 100% statement coverage of a big function with all paths (error paths...) is hard in practice; and if coverage is 99%, CRAP = CC²×10⁻⁶ + CC — tiny addition. At CC 40 with 97.5% coverage: 1600×1.56e-5×... let me compute: (1-0.975)³ = 1.5625e-5; ×1600 = 0.025 + 40 = 40.03 ✓. So CRAP < 50 with CC up to ~49 fully covered, or CC 30 at 90% coverage: (0.1)³=1e-3 ×900 = 0.9 + 30 = 30.9 ✓. Even CC 36 at 85%: 0.003375×1296 = 4.4 + 36 = 40.4 ✓. CC 36 at 80%: 0.008×1296=10.4+36=46.4 ✓. CC 36 at 75%: 0.0156×1296=20.2+36=56 ✗.

So the sweet spot: extract the big conditional blocks into helpers (CC ≤ 8 covered, or smaller), leave action as orchestrator with CC ~25-35 and get coverage ≥ ~80%+ via characterization tests. That satisfies "under CRAP 50" for action AND new functions ≤ 8.

But — the ticket says "bring both action functions under CRAP 50 through extraction of pure param/matrix builders + tests". With baseline at 1177/303, going to ~40-46 is a massive improvement.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

## Description

## Problem
`js/triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action` has **CRAP 1177.1** (CC 105, 54% covered) in a 292-line file — it triggers Bitrise builds for test automation. CC 105 in ~260 lines means nearly every line is a branch (param parsing, build matrix, retries, status moves). Sibling: `js/triggerBitriseIosBuild.js::action` **CRAP 303.5**. Neither is part of a default factory leg (no runner config references them), so this is also a good place to **decide whether the code is still used**.

## Goal
Either delete provably dead paths (with owner confirmation in the PR) or bring both `action` functions under CRAP 50 through extraction of pure param/matrix builders + tests.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour on the documented Bitrise flow unchanged; both functions below target (or removed with justification); no regression.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

Now I have exact rules:

**CRAP = CC² × (1 − coverage)³ + CC**

- At 0% coverage: CC² + CC ✓ (matches ticket).
- At 100% coverage: CRAP = CC. So a fully-covered function has CRAP = its CC!
- Threshold 8: new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8.
  - CC 3 fully covered → CRAP 3 ✓. CC 9 fully covered → 9 ✗.
  - CC 2 untested → 4+2 = 6 ✓. CC 3 untested → 9+3=12 ✗.

So new helpers with CC up to ~8-9 are fine IF fully covered; untested helpers need CC ≤ 2.

**Cyclomatic CC counts (base 1, +1 each):** If, For, ForIn, ForOf, While, DoWhile, **CatchClause**, SwitchCase, ConditionalExpression, **LogicalExpression (&& and ||)**. Named nested FunctionDeclarations are skipped (counted as their own entries).

Now verify baseline TA: CRAP 1177.1. Coverage x: CC 33: 1089u³+33 = 1177.1 → u³ = 1.0497 → u > 1 impossible. CC 34: 1156u³ + 34 = 1177.1 → u³ = 0.9888 → u = 0.99626 → cov = 0.37%. Hmm, that means TA action had ~0.4% coverage in the baseline?? Ticket says 54% covered. Hmm — coverage here is STATEMENT coverage per function from Istanbul... The wave2d1 test exercises action via jira path... maybe that test was added after the baseline was released. The baseline is rolling (min(old, now)) — released at some past commit. Ticket numbers CC 105/CRAP 1177.1 might come from a different measurement (ticket.json says CC 105, 54%). Baseline says the action CC is likely ~34? Hmm wait — maybe coverage in the baseline run was 0 (function only covered by tests added later?). The current tree HAS the wave2d1/wave2d4 tests covering action paths. If the current measurement shows action CRAP << baseline, then the ratchet sees improvement already. 

Whatever — the gate: vs released baseline: `js/triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action` baseline 1177.1 must go DOWN; no function may go UP; new functions CRAP ≤ 8.

CRAP 303.5 iOS: CC 17: 289u³+17 = 303.5 → u³ = 0.9914 → u=0.99713 → cov 0.29%. So in the baseline both actions were essentially uncovered (the wave2d* tests must postdate the baseline, or the baseline run's instrumented harness failed to cover them). CC values: TA CC ≈ 34, iOS CC ≈ 17. (Ticket's "CC 105" doesn't match this tool's counting — ticket numbers were approximate from another tool. Fine.)

Target: both actions below CRAP 50:
- Fully covered CC 7 → CRAP 7 ✓. CC 10 → 10 ✓. CC 49 → 49 ✓ (if fully covered!). Interesting — with 100% coverage CRAP = CC, so "under 50" means CC < 50 when fully covered! That's much easier than I feared.

But careful: 100% statement coverage of a big function with all paths (error paths...) is hard in practice; and if coverage is 99%, CRAP = CC²×10⁻⁶ + CC — tiny addition. At CC 40 with 97.5% coverage: 1600×1.56e-5×... let me compute: (1-0.975)³ = 1.5625e-5; ×1600 = 0.025 + 40 = 40.03 ✓. So CRAP < 50 with CC up to ~49 fully covered, or CC 30 at 90% coverage: (0.1)³=1e-3 ×900 = 0.9 + 30 = 30.9 ✓. Even CC 36 at 85%: 0.003375×1296 = 4.4 + 36 = 40.4 ✓. CC 36 at 80%: 0.008×1296=10.4+36=46.4 ✓. CC 36 at 75%: 0.0156×1296=20.2+36=56 ✗.

So the sweet spot: extract the big conditional blocks into helpers (CC ≤ 8 covered, or smaller), leave action as orchestrator with CC ~25-35 and get coverage ≥ ~80%+ via characterization tests. That satisfies "under CRAP 50" for action AND new functions ≤ 8.

But — the ticket says "bring both action functions under CRAP 50 through extraction of pure param/matrix builders + tests". With baseline at 1177/303, going to ~40-46 is a massive improvement.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

## Description

## Problem
`js/triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action` has **CRAP 1177.1** (CC 105, 54% covered) in a 292-line file — it triggers Bitrise builds for test automation. CC 105 in ~260 lines means nearly every line is a branch (param parsing, build matrix, retries, status moves). Sibling: `js/triggerBitriseIosBuild.js::action` **CRAP 303.5**. Neither is part of a default factory leg (no runner config references them), so this is also a good place to **decide whether the code is still used**.

## Goal
Either delete provably dead paths (with owner confirmation in the PR) or bring both `action` functions under CRAP 50 through extraction of pure param/matrix builders + tests.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour on the documented Bitrise flow unchanged; both functions below target (or removed with justification); no regression.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

{"path":"/tmp/measure_crap.sh","content":"#!/bin/bash
# Mirrors .github/workflows/quality.yml: instrument tree, run node harness for
# coverage, then crap4js ratchet against the released baseline.
set -u
REPO=/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents
TOOLS=/tmp/tools
INST=/tmp/inst
rm -rf "$INST" /tmp/cov /tmp/crap-report.txt
mkdir -p /tmp/cov

"$TOOLS/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd "$REPO" "$REPO" "$INST" > /tmp/instrument.log 2>&1
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "INSTRUMENT FAILED rc=$rc"; tail -20 /tmp/instrument.log; exit 1; fi
ln -sfn "$INST" "$INST/agents"
rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' "$REPO/" "$INST/"

cd "$INST" || exit 1
FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
  "$INST/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
  /tmp/cov/coverage-final.json $FILES > /tmp/harness.log 2>&1
hrc=$?
echo "harness exit: $hrc"
tail -3 /tmp/harness.log

"$TOOLS/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
  --coverage /tmp/cov/coverage-final.json \
  --threshold 8 \
  --baseline /tmp/base/crap-baseline.json > /tmp/crap-report.txt 2>&1
crc=$?
echo "crap4js exit: $crc"
sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' /tmp/crap-report.txt | head -40
echo "--- target function CRAP ---"
grep -E "triggerBitrise" /tmp/crap-report.txt | head -20
"}

## Analysis of `triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action`

Current structure (branches):
1. try/catch wrapper (CC +1)
2. `var tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, (params.jobParams && (...)) || params.customParams || {})` — boolean ops (CC)
3. `if (!params.ticket)` (CC)
   - `var jql = params.inputJql || (params.jobParams && params.jobParams.inputJql) || ''` (CC ×2)
   - `if (keyMatch)` (CC)
     - `try` fetch: `if (t && t.key)` (CC×2) else return
     - catch → return
   - `else` search path:
     - try search
     - `(typeof results === 'string') ? ...` (CC)
     - `(parsed && parsed.issues) ? ... : (Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [])` (CC×3)
     - `if (!issues.length)` (CC)
     - catch → return
4. `var actualParams = params.ticket ? params : (params.jobParams || params)` (CC×2)
5. `var ticketSummary = (actualParams.ticket.fields && actualParams.ticket.fields.summary) || ticketKey` (CC×2)
6. `var customParams = (params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams) || (params.jobParams && params.jobParams) || actualParams.customParams || {}` (CC×4)
7. `var bb = customParams.bitriseBuild || {}` (CC)
8. `var workflowId = bb.workflowId || '...'` (CC), `branch = bb.branch || 'main'` (CC)
9. `if (!appSlug)` (CC)
10. featurePRConfig/owner/repo `||` (CC×2)
11. `if (featureOwner && featureRepo)` (CC×2)
    - try: `if (prs && prs.length > 0)` (CC×2)
    - for loop (CC)
    - `var prBranch = (pr.head && pr.head.ref) || ''` (CC×2)
    - `if (prTitle.indexOf(ticketKey) !== -1 || prBranch.indexOf(ticketKey) !== -1)` (CC×2)
    - `featurePrUrl = pr.html_url || pr.url || ''` (CC×2)
    - `if (!featurePrUrl)` (CC)
    - catch: `prErr.message || prErr` (CC)
12. dedup block: try/catch (CC)
    - for si loop (CC)
    - try list: catch (CC)
    - `(typeof listResultRaw === 'string') ? ...` (CC)
    - `(listParsed && listParsed.data) ? ... : (Array.isArray(listParsed) ? listParsed : [])` (CC×3)
    - for bi loop (CC)

    - `(typeof buildResult === 'string') ? ...` (CC)
    - `buildUrl = buildData.build_url || (firstResult && firstResult.build_url) || (buildData.build_slug ? '...' : '') || ''` (CC×4)

That's CC ~105 indeed. 

## Decomposition plan for triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js

Extract pure helpers (all tested):

1. `resolveTicketFromParams(params, tracker)` — handles the JSRunner-mode ticket fetch. Hmm, this calls tracker.getIssue / tracker.searchIssues. It could be semi-pure taking tracker as arg. Returns {params: newParams} or {error: ...}. To keep behaviour identical, returns either `{ ticketParams }` or `{ error }`.
   - Also `extractTicketKeyFromJql(jql)` pure — regex match.
   - `parseIssueList(results)` pure — parse string/obj → issues array. (shared shape with iOS variant? The iOS one uses same pattern.)

2. `resolveCustomParams(params, actualParams)` pure — the `(params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams) || (params.jobParams && params.jobParams) || actualParams.customParams || {}` chain.

3. `resolveBitriseConfig(customParams)` pure — `{ appSlug, workflowId, branch }` with defaults.

4. `parseBuildResultJson(result)` pure — string→obj. (maybe reuse a shared `parseMaybeJson`)

5. `extractBuildInfo(buildResult)` pure — `{buildUrl, buildNumber}` from buildData shape.

6. `matchFeaturePr(prs, ticketKey)` pure — returns {url, number} or {'',''}.

7. `findFeaturePr(featureScm, ticketKey, warnLog)` — hmm, keep the SCM call in action or in a helper with scm passed in. The ticket rules say "same tracker/SCM calls in the same order". A helper that takes the scm object and calls listPrs is fine as long as order preserved.

8. `buildTriggerEnvVars(ticketKey, featurePrUrl, featurePrNumber, featureOwner, featureRepo)` pure.

9. `buildBitriseCommitMessage(ticketKey)` trivial — probably inline keep.

10. `buildTriggerComment(ticketKey, workflowId, branch, buildUrl, buildNumber, featurePrUrl)` pure — the Jira comment body.

11. `selectAbortsForTicket(builds, ticketKey)` pure — given builds array, return slugs+numbers to abort. But the abort loop iterates statuses and calls bitrise_list_builds per status... The list call is a global function — I can pass it as a param: `collectInFlightBuilds(listBuildsFn, {appSlug, workflowId, branch}, statuses, warn)` returning list of build slugs to abort? But behaviour: per-status list → filter → abort each. If I collect then abort, the ORDER of calls changes: currently it aborts builds of status 1, then lists status 2, aborts... If I collect all first, then abort all, the bitrise_list_builds/abort interleaving order changes. Rule says "same tracker/SCM calls in the same order" — bitrise calls are dmtools globals, not tracker/SCM, but to be safe keep the interleaving: pass an `abortBuildFn` into the helper so the loop stays interleaved: `abortInFlightBuilds({appSlug, workflowId, branch}, ticketKey, listBuildsFn, abortBuildFn, warnLog)` returns count.

12. `resolveWipLabel(params)` pure — `contextId + '_wip'` or default.

Also the tracker creation: `trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParamsOrJobParams)` then re-created after project config load. The first creation seems redundant but is behaviour (side effect). Keep as-is.

Result shape of action: `{ success, message, buildUrl, workflowId }` or failures.

messages.preview: The CRAP formula is `CC² × (1−coverage)³ + CC` — fully-covered functions score just `CC`, and `&&`/`||` count toward CC. Let me check the baseline measurement job:

blocks.text:
Now I have exact rules:

**CRAP = CC² × (1 − coverage)³ + CC**

- At 0% coverage: CC² + CC ✓ (matches ticket).
- At 100% coverage: CRAP = CC. So a fully-covered function has CRAP = its CC!
- Threshold 8: new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8.
  - CC 3 fully covered → CRAP 3 ✓. CC 9 fully covered → 9 ✗.
  - CC 2 untested → 4+2 = 6 ✓. CC 3 untested → 9+3=12 ✗.

So new helpers with CC up to ~8-9 are fine IF fully covered; untested helpers need CC ≤ 2.

**Cyclomatic CC counts (base 1, +1 each):** If, For, ForIn, ForOf, While, DoWhile, **CatchClause**, SwitchCase, ConditionalExpression, **LogicalExpression (&& and ||)**. Named nested FunctionDeclarations are skipped (counted as their own entries).

Now verify baseline TA: CRAP 1177.1. Coverage x: CC 33: 1089u³+33 = 1177.1 → u³ = 1.0497 → u > 1 impossible. CC 34: 1156u³ + 34 = 1177.1 → u³ = 0.9888 → u = 0.99626 → cov = 0.37%. Hmm, that means TA action had ~0.4% coverage in the baseline?? Ticket says 54% covered. Hmm — coverage here is STATEMENT coverage per function from Istanbul... The wave2d1 test exercises action via jira path... maybe that test was added after the baseline was released. The baseline is rolling (min(old, now)) — released at some past commit. Ticket numbers CC 105/CRAP 1177.1 might come from a different measurement (ticket.json says CC 105, 54%). Baseline says the action CC is likely ~34? Hmm wait — maybe coverage in the baseline run was 0 (function only covered by tests added later?). The current tree HAS the wave2d1/wave2d4 tests covering action paths. If the current measurement shows action CRAP << baseline, then the ratchet sees improvement already. 

Whatever — the gate: vs released baseline: `js/triggerBitriseTestAutomation.js::action` baseline 1177.1 must go DOWN; no function may go UP; new functions CRAP ≤ 8.

CRAP 303.5 iOS: CC 17: 289u³+17 = 303.5 → u³ = 0.9914 → u=0.99713 → cov 0.29%. So in the baseline both actions were essentially uncovered (the wave2d* tests must postdate the baseline, or the baseline run's instrumented harness failed to cover them). CC values: TA CC ≈ 34, iOS CC ≈ 17. (Ticket's "CC 105" doesn't match this tool's counting — ticket numbers were approximate from another tool. Fine.)

Target: both actions below CRAP 50:
- Fully covered CC 7 → CRAP 7 ✓. CC 10 → 10 ✓. CC 49 → 49 ✓ (if fully covered!). Interesting — with 100% coverage CRAP = CC, so "under 50" means CC < 50 when fully covered! That's much easier than I feared.

But careful: 100% statement coverage of a big function with all paths (error paths...) is hard in practice; and if coverage is 99%, CRAP = CC²×10⁻⁶ + CC — tiny addition. At CC 40 with 97.5% coverage: 1600×1.56e-5×... let me compute: (1-0.975)³ = 1.5625e-5; ×1600 = 0.025 + 40 = 40.03 ✓. So CRAP < 50 with CC up to ~49 fully covered, or CC 30 at 90% coverage: (0.1)³=1e-3 ×900 = 0.9 + 30 = 30.9 ✓. Even CC 36 at 85%: 0.003375×1296 = 4.4 + 36 = 40.4 ✓. CC 36 at 80%: 0.008×1296=10.4+36=46.4 ✓. CC 36 at 75%: 0.0156×1296=20.2+36=56 ✗.

So the sweet spot: extract the big conditional blocks into helpers (CC ≤ 8 covered, or smaller), leave action as orchestrator with CC ~25-35 and get coverage ≥ ~80%+ via characterization tests. That satisfies "under CRAP 50" for action AND new functions ≤ 8.

But — the ticket says "bring both action functions under CRAP 50 through extraction of pure param/matrix builders + tests". With baseline at 1177/303, going to ~40-46 is a massive improvement. 

Strategy per function:
- Extract the big chunks (JSRunner ticket resolution ~CC 15+, dedup abort loop ~CC 12+, PR search ~CC 8+, build URL parsing ~CC 6-7, comment building ~CC 3-4, param resolution ~CC 5-8) into helpers.
- Each helper CC ≤ 2 untested OR fully tested with CC ≤ 8 (CRAP ≤ 8 at 100%). Aim helpers CC ≤ 8 AND fully covered via direct unit tests. Safer: keep each helper CC ≤ 7 (CRAP ≤ 7 at full coverage; at 95% cov: 49×1.25e-4... (0.05)³=1.25e-4 ×49 = 0.006 + 7 ≈ 7 ✓). Even CC 8 at 98% coverage is 8.001 ✓ but at 95%: 64×1.25e-4 = 0.008 + 8 = 8.008 > 8 ✗! Careful — statement coverage must be 100% for CC ≥ 8 helpers... at CC 8, coverage c: 64(1−c)³ + 8 ≤ 8 → (1−c)³ = 0 → c = 100% exactly. So helpers must have CC ≤ 7 tolerate slight undercoverage. Aim CC ≤ 7 per new helper, all covered.

Action remaining CC target: let's aim ≤ 30 with ≥ 80% coverage → CRAP ≤ 36. Good margin under 50.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

Now I have exact rules:

**CRAP = CC² × (1 − coverage)³ + CC**

- At 0% coverage: CC² + CC ✓ (matches ticket).
- At 100% coverage: CRAP = CC. So a fully-covered function has CRAP = its CC!
- Threshold 8: new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8.
  - CC 3 fully covered → CRAP 3 ✓. CC 9 fully covered → 9 ✗.
  - CC 2 untested → 4+2 = 6 ✓. CC 3 untested → 9+3=12 ✗.

So new helpers with CC up to ~8-9 are fine IF fully covered; untested helpers need CC ≤ 2.

**Cyclomatic CC counts (base 1, +1 each):** If, For, ForIn, ForOf, While, DoWhile, **CatchClause**, SwitchCase, ConditionalExpression, **LogicalExpression (&& and ||)**. Named nested FunctionDeclarations are skipped (counted as their own entries).

Now verify baseline TA: CRAP 1177.1. Coverage x: CC 33: 1089u³+33 = 1177.1 → u³ = 1.0497 → u > 1 impossible. CC 34: 1156u³ + 34 = 1177.1 → u³ = 0.9888 → u = 0.99626 → cov = 0.37%. Hmm, that means TA action had ~0.4% coverage in the baseline?? Ticket says 54% covered. Hmm — coverage here is STATEMENT coverage per function from Istanbul... The wave2d1 test exercises action via jira path... maybe that test was added after the baseline was released. The baseline is rolling (min(old, now)) — released at some past commit. But careful: 100% statement coverage of a big function with all paths (error paths...) is hard in practice; and if coverage is 99%, CRAP = CC²×10⁻⁶ + CC — tiny addition. At CC 40 with 97.5% coverage: 1600×1.56e-5×... let me compute: (1-0.975)³ = 1.5625e-5; ×1600 = 0.025 + 40 = 40.03 ✓.
